source_text: Quod utrumque fecit Manichaeus, qui commentatus in carne malum esse naturaliter, dixit in Christo non fuisse carnem, ne confiteretur in eo fuisse iniquitatem.
pass_a_gloss: Which both Manichaeus did, who, having invented that there is evil in the flesh naturally, said there was not flesh in Christ, lest he confess that iniquity had been in him.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Manichaeus did both. Having invented the claim that evil exists naturally in flesh, he said that there was no flesh in Christ, to avoid confessing that there was injustice in him.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
